steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The biological approach assumes all behaviour has a physical cause in the brain, nervous system, genes and biochemistry. Behaviour can be explained in terms of biological structures and processes.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Genetic basis of behaviour: genes inherited from parents influence characteristics. Twin studies compare MZ (identical, 100% genes shared) with DZ (fraternal, 50% shared) twins. If MZ concordance is higher, genetic influence is likely. Example: McGuffin et al. found 37% MZ vs 15% DZ concordance for depression.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evolution and behaviour: behaviours that enhanced survival and reproduction were naturally selected. Evolutionary explanations account for: fight-or-flight (adaptive for physical threats), attachment (infants who stayed close to caregivers survived), phobias (fear of snakes/spiders was adaptive).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Neurochemistry: neurotransmitters influence mood and behaviour. Serotonin (mood, aggression), dopamine (reward, motivation), adrenaline (fight-or-flight). Imbalances are linked to mental health conditions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the key assumptions of the biological approach and explain how genes influence behaviour. | Evaluate the biological approach, considering its strengths and limitations. | Discuss whether behaviour is determined by biology, referring to the nature-nurture debate.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Biological approach: behaviour = GENES + BRAIN + NEUROCHEMISTRY + EVOLUTION. MZ twins share 100% genes. DZ share 50%. Higher MZ concordance = genetic influence. Strengths = scientific + practical treatments. Weaknesses = reductionist + deterministic + ignores environment.
